name: Thinkific
tagline: Host a structured course with lessons, progress, and simple quizzes

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited courses; 10,000 current students; 100 GB video uploads/month; 1 community with 5 spaces; 5 digital downloads; 5 coaching/webinar products; 1 admin

tiers.name: Start
tiers.limits: Unlimited courses; 10,000 current students; 200 GB video uploads/month; 1 community with 10 spaces; unlimited downloads/coaching products; 2 admins

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.limits: Unlimited courses; 10,000 current students; 400 GB video uploads/month; 3 communities with 20 spaces each; 6 admins

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Custom current-student allowance; unlimited courses, communities, and spaces; video allowance starts at 7,500 GB/month

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual prices shown as effective monthly rates; about 25% lower)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Branded mobile app is $199/month. Thinkific Payments starts at 2.9%+$0.30, plus 1.5% for international cards, 1% FX, 0.7% for subscriptions/payment plans, 0.5% tax/VAT service, and 0.4% invoicing up to $5; instant payout is 1.5%. Third-party gateway fees are 5% Basic, 2% Start, 1% Grow, and 0% on the first $1M/year on Plus.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Thinkific, host a structured course with lessons, progress, and simple quizzes. The hard boundary is course builder, payments, communities, apps, integrations, and support, plus payments, tax, distribution, and operations.
coreLoopDIY: Host a structured course with lessons, progress tracking, and simple quizzes, sell it from a user-owned storefront, deliver purchased lessons, and manage customers.
whatYouLose: course builder, payments, communities, apps, integrations, and support
ongoingBurden: checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Thinkific because creators pay to outsource the dangerous and tedious parts around money, delivery, tax, and customer access. The recurring cost buys checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Medusa
priorArt.desc: Active open-source commerce platform with modular checkout and fulfillment primitives.

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: A modern self-hosted course site with lessons, quizzes, drip and progress; email and storage need configuring.

facts.install: Docker Compose, with SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL set before first start
facts.dataFormat: Application records in MongoDB; production media uploads use MediaLit plus S3-compatible object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: CourseLit's assessment/reporting ecosystem is less mature than Thinkific's and production email/storage are the owner's job.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker starts the app, but a production setup also needs SMTP for email login and MediaLit/S3-compatible storage for uploads

alternatives.name: Frappe Learning
alternatives.desc: Structured courses, lessons, progress, quizzes and certificates without a licence bill; Docker remains.

facts.install: Run Frappe's easy-install script or the official Docker Compose deployment
facts.dataFormat: Course and user records in the Frappe/MariaDB site database; public/private site files on disk, while video lessons commonly embed external hosts
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe Learning has a less mature hosted creator workflow and requires infrastructure, email and payment setup.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting still needs Docker or a Frappe server, DNS/SSL and email; payments require separate gateway configuration

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: Lessons, progress and quizzes with decades of scars and capabilities.

facts.install: Upload the PHP release to a web server, create a database and moodledata directory, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Courses, users, grades and settings in SQL; uploaded files in the separate moodledata directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Moodle is far heavier to operate and less polished for a solo creator even though its LMS depth is greater.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and database requirements, protected writable storage, cron, SMTP, backups and upgrades are all the operator's responsibility

alternatives.name: Odoo Community
alternatives.desc: Paid courses, lessons, quizzes and progress inside a giant business suite; overkill arrives preinstalled.

facts.install: Use Odoo's packaged installer, source install or Docker image, backed by PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Business and website records in PostgreSQL; uploaded attachments in Odoo's filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo is operational overkill and offers a less focused course-authoring and learner experience than Thinkific.
facts.setupBlocker: A production deployment needs PostgreSQL, workers/reverse proxy configuration, backups and ongoing administration of a very large suite

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: One structured course with lessons and quizzes on a hosted free plan; one is the operative number.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, funnels, course/community content, orders, emails and uploaded files in systeme.io's vendor-managed cloud; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan supports only one course and offers less mature learning analytics, authoring and assessment control than Thinkific.
facts.setupBlocker: Selling requires connecting a payment gateway; the free plan is capped at 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, one community and one custom domain

alternatives.name: Tutor LMS
alternatives.desc: WordPress courses, progress and quizzes for free; the surrounding plugin ecosystem will introduce itself.

facts.install: Install from WordPress Plugins → Add New, then run Tutor LMS's setup wizard
facts.dataFormat: Courses, enrollments and settings in the WordPress database; lesson media in the WordPress Media Library
facts.gapVsPaid: Tutor LMS trades Thinkific's hosted simplicity for WordPress/plugin maintenance, while several advanced course features sit outside the free core.
facts.setupBlocker: It first requires a maintained WordPress site, and subscriptions, certificates, assignments, drip content and several integrations sit outside the free core

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Selling access is not the same as delivering lessons, progress and quizzes.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a single-creator storefront DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Thinkific in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Stripe Checkout, and S3-compatible storage; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a structured course with lessons, progress tracking, and simple quizzes, sell it from a user-owned storefront, deliver purchased lessons, and manage customers.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement products, variants, prices, files or lessons, coupons, customers, orders, and entitlements.
Use Stripe-hosted Checkout and verify every webhook signature and idempotency key.
Grant access only after confirmed payment and revoke it on refund or chargeback.
Create a customer library with signed short-lived download or lesson URLs.
Add order search, resend receipt, refund handoff, export, and an immutable event log.
Document taxes as the creator's responsibility and do not calculate unsupported jurisdictions.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out merchant-of-record tax remittance.
Deliberately leave out a buyer marketplace or affiliate network.
Deliberately leave out advanced communities, certificates, mobile apps, and enterprise learning features.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
